ai.definition: On-Device SLMs are small language models that have been optimized to run efficiently on edge devices equipped with NPUs (Neural Processing Units). These models are designed to be lightweight and power-efficient while maintaining a reasonable level of performance.
ai.howItWorks: These models achieve efficiency through techniques such as quantization, which reduces the precision of weights in neural networks, and distillation, where knowledge from larger models is transferred into smaller ones. This allows them to run effectively on edge devices without requiring cloud connectivity or significant computational resources.
ai.problemSolved: On-Device SLMs address the challenges of privacy concerns, high latency, and energy consumption associated with traditional cloud-based language processing by enabling local computation and decision-making.
ai.manufacturing: Manufacturing involves optimizing the model architecture for NPUs, which requires specialized knowledge in both machine learning and hardware design. The process also includes rigorous testing to ensure that the models meet performance and efficiency requirements.
ai.buildProcess: The build process starts with training large language models on cloud infrastructure, followed by quantization and distillation techniques to reduce their size and complexity. These smaller models are then fine-tuned for specific tasks before being deployed onto edge devices.
ai.costDrivers: Cost drivers include the computational resources required for model training, optimization tools, and testing frameworks. Additionally, the cost of developing specialized hardware for NPUs can be significant.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook is positive as more devices are equipped with NPUs, creating a growing market for on-device SLMs.
ai.regulation: Current regulations around data privacy and AI ethics may impact the adoption of on-device SLMs. Compliance with these regulations will be crucial for widespread acceptance.
ai.risks: Risks include potential performance degradation when models are quantized or distilled, as well as challenges in maintaining model accuracy while reducing size.
ai.profitability: Profitability is likely to increase as more companies adopt edge computing strategies and demand for privacy-preserving solutions grows.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development will focus on improving model efficiency without sacrificing performance, expanding use cases beyond privacy, and integrating with other edge technologies like IoT devices.
ai.energyRequirements: Field units draw low hundreds of watts; fabrication is energy-intensive due to vacuum baking.

glossary.def: Neural Processing Unit, specialized hardware for accelerating machine learning tasks.
The process of reducing the precision of weights in neural networks to make them more efficient and smaller.
A technique where knowledge from larger models is transferred into smaller ones, resulting in a model that can run efficiently on edge devices.

subsystems.name: Compact model architecture
subsystems.role: a transformer small enough to fit a phone's memory budget, usually 1–8 billion parameters.

subsystems.name: Compression pipeline
subsystems.role: shrinks a big model's knowledge into weights the device can hold and move quickly.

subsystems.name: On-device runtime
subsystems.role: turns a prompt into streamed tokens using as little power as possible.

subsystems.name: NPU and accelerators
subsystems.role: the silicon that does the matrix maths.

subsystems.name: Memory and storage
subsystems.role: feeds weights to the NPU fast enough to matter.

subsystems.name: OS integration and privacy layer
subsystems.role: exposes the model to apps without sending data anywhere.

buildSteps.title: Set the memory budget
buildSteps.detail: Decide the target device class, then work backwards from how much RAM and bandwidth the model may use, since that caps parameter count.

buildSteps.title: Distil from a larger teacher
buildSteps.detail: Train the small model to imitate the outputs and internal distributions of a much bigger frontier model, using the teacher to label or rank data.

buildSteps.title: Post-train for instruction and safety
buildSteps.detail: Fine-tune on curated instructions and preference data, and add refusal behaviour so the model behaves predictably in a consumer product.

buildSteps.title: Quantize the weights
buildSteps.detail: Calibrate activations on representative prompts, then compress weights to 8 or 4 bits; quantization-aware training recovers accuracy lost at very low bit widths.

buildSteps.title: Lower the graph to the NPU
buildSteps.detail: A compiler fuses operations, tiles them to the accelerator's on-chip memory, and emits kernels; unsupported operations fall back to CPU or GPU.

buildSteps.title: Build the runtime
buildSteps.detail: Add a tokenizer, a KV cache that grows and is reused across turns, streaming output, and memory-mapped loading so the model starts without a long copy.

buildSteps.title: Package for the platform
buildSteps.detail: Ship the model as an OS component or app library with versioning, so it can be updated and rolled back independently of the app.

buildSteps.title: Evaluate on real hardware
buildSteps.detail: Measure time to first token, tokens per second, peak memory, accuracy regression against the unquantized model, and battery/thermal behaviour over long sessions.

buildSteps.title: Ship and keep measuring
buildSteps.detail: Deploy to devices, watch for failures on old or low-memory hardware, and retrain when the next NPU generation arrives.

prerequisites.why: small models are scaled-down versions of the same design, so all the scaling tricks apply directly.
without 4-bit weights a useful model will not fit in a phone's memory alongside the operating system.
it is how a tiny model inherits capability from a much larger one rather than learning everything from scratch.
dedicated INT8/INT4 hardware runs inference several times more efficiently than a CPU or GPU.
phones move data at tens of gigabytes per second, so decode is memory-bound and bandwidth, not compute, is often the real limit.
they translate trained models into kernels each vendor's accelerator can actually execute.

pathway.milestone: 1–8 billion parameter models running on flagship phones and laptops for summarisation, dictation and notification triage
pathway.unlocks: useful language features that work offline and never leave the device.

pathway.milestone: on-device personalisation through small adapters trained or selected locally
pathway.unlocks: assistants that adapt to a person's writing and habits without uploading their data.

pathway.milestone: multi-modal small models and local retrieval over the user's own files
pathway.unlocks: question answering over photos, documents and messages entirely on the device.

pathway.milestone: agentic on-device assistants that call local tools under a strict power budget
pathway.unlocks: task automation with privacy as a default rather than a setting.
